from_speaker: I can’t imagine anyone spending $300 a year on a search product
aggressively serving ads to make up the difference
our_interpretation: Read this as a forecast of commercially unlikely behavior, rather than a claim about the author's imagination.
The surrounding discussion limits the target to OpenAI's search product and its successor within ChatGPT.
The price clause concerns customers paying $300 per year for search. A multipurpose subscription priced above that amount does not establish how much customers pay specifically for search.
For the advertising antecedent, paid access to a bundle containing search counts as OpenAI charging. This does not attribute the entire subscription price to search.
The ordinary reading of aggressively serving ads is frequent or intrusive advertising used substantially to supplement subscription income. Merely introducing advertisements is insufficient.
The dollar figure describes hypothetical customer spending, not a reported accounting measure. No accounting basis is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would need to establish both the absence of customers paying $300 annually for the search offering and, if OpenAI charges, the absence of aggressive advertising throughout the relevant commercial opportunity. With no deadline, a temporary absence cannot conclusively support these predictions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Verified purchases attributable to search at $300 per year, or clear evidence that a paid search offering routinely serves frequent or intrusive advertisements to supplement subscription income, would contradict the relevant clause. Advertising on a free tier alone or the price of a multipurpose bundle is insufficient.
